query: Mexico ended 2014 with general government debt of 48.1 percent of GDP and a cyclically adjusted primary balance of -1.4 percent of GDP. Treat it as an emerging market economy. What cyclically adjusted primary balance would it have to reach by 2020 and then maintain through 2030 for its debt to come down to the long-term benchmark for emerging market economies by 2030? Give that level and the change relative to 2014, in percent of GDP. Use IMF World Economic Outlook (October 2025) GDP and fiscal outturns for its growth and interest costs.

text.text: Identifies the Fiscal Monitor approach to illustrative fiscal adjustment needs for a long-term debt target: solve for the cyclically adjusted primary balance that, held constant over 2020-2030 after a gradual adjustment over 2016-2020 (taken as linear), brings debt to 40 percent of GDP by 2030 for an emerging market economy (or holds it at the end-2014 ratio if that is already lower), using a debt recursion in which the interest-growth differential rises linearly from its 2014 level to 1 percentage point by 2028.
text.accept: full = names the long-term debt-target adjustment-needs exercise (Fiscal Monitor Statistical Appendix, tables 'Illustrative Adjustment Needs Based on Long-Term Debt Targets') and applies the 40 percent EM target with the stated path and differential; partial = right idea (primary balance needed to reach a debt target by 2030) but with a different target, path or constant differential; no = debt-stabilising balance, S1/S2 gap or a fiscal-rule calibration.

text.text: Concludes that the country must raise its cyclically adjusted primary balance above its 2014 level (a tightening of about 2.5 points of GDP).
text.accept: full = direction (tightening) stated and consistent with the reported number; partial = direction right without magnitude; no = wrong direction.

data.text: Uses nominal GDP (growth) and the interest bill implied by the primary and overall balances relative to previous-year debt from the WEO October 2025 vintage (GGXONLB_NGDP, GGXCNL_NGDP, GGXWDG_NGDP, NGDP) together with the end-2014 debt and CAPB given in the question.
data.accept: full = growth, interest and the given 2014 positions used; partial = a single assumed r-g or growth path; no = unrelated series.

computation.text: Mexico: a cyclically adjusted primary balance of about 1.1% of GDP held over 2020-30 (published Fiscal Monitor value 1.3).
computation.accept: full = within 1 of 1.1; partial = correct sign and within 2; no = otherwise. Starting differential from WEO Oct 2025 outturn; parameters per the grading note.

computation.text: Mexico: change of about +2.5 points of GDP relative to the end-2014 CAPB of -1.4%.
computation.accept: full = within 1 of 2.5; partial = correct sign and within 2; no = otherwise.

computation.text: Debt target used: 40.0% of GDP in 2030.
computation.accept: full = within 0.1 of 40; partial = correct sign and within 0.2; no = otherwise.

grading.note: Level of the constant CAPB over 2020-30 and its change from 2014, in percentage points of GDP. Tolerance 1.0 pp: the recomputation with WEO Oct 2025 outturn differs from the Fiscal Monitor April 2014 published column by -0.24 pp for this country (published 1.3, recomputed 1.06); across the 26 EMs 21 are within 1 pp.

provenance.method_text: Fiscal Monitor Statistical Appendix, 'Illustrative Adjustment Needs Based on Long-Term Debt Targets', notes on emerging markets (Table 14 in the April 2014 issue)

method_doc_note: Verified on the corpus text 2026-10-30. All three issues carry the emerging-market rule in the note of their statistical table: FM April 2014 (a9063586) Table 14 note 3, block 955; FM October 2014 (49b36e52) Table 25 note 3, block 935 (identical wording: 40 percent target, CAPB follows projections to 2015, adjusts gradually 2016-2020, constant to 2030, r-g linear from 2014 level to 1 by 2028); FM October 2013 (9a9aeb9c) Table 14 note 3, block 832 (same rule one year earlier: 2011-14 projections, gradual 2015-2020, r-g to 1 by 2027). The three tables also print the answer: April 2014 Table 14 block 950 (the gold report), October 2014 Table 25 block 930 (same base year, updated numbers: for example Poland CAPB 2020-30 1.2 against 1.3, within the 1.0 tolerance) and October 2013 Table 14 block 827 (2013 base). WITHHOLDING: remove the table blocks 950 (April 2014), 930 (October 2014, and Table 24a block 917) and 827 (October 2013, and Table 13a block 815); keep the note blocks 955, 935, 832 and 942/923/821 so the rule stays in the corpus. Whole-document withholding of a9063586 and 49b36e52 would leave only the 2013 vintage for the rule. The word 'linearly' in the document applies to the interest-growth differential only; the CAPB path is 'gradual', and the gold's linear shape is an assumption (changes the answer by up to 1.1 points for India, under 0.7 for the others tested).
distractors: Debt-stabilising primary balance (holds the ratio constant, no debt target)
Fiscal sustainability gaps (S1/S2 type indicators over a long or infinite horizon)
Calibration of a fiscal rule (debt anchor with a safety margin, deficit ceiling)
Adjustment needed to reach the 60 percent advanced-economy benchmark (wrong target and group for an emerging market)
Decomposition of the change in the debt ratio (accounting of past debt changes, no forward target)
Stress test of the debt path (shock scenarios rather than a required adjustment)

strictness.overall: strict (emerging-market rule fully specified); free only the 2014 starting differential (data)

parameters.debt_target: strict: 40 percent of GDP in 2030 for emerging markets (60 for advanced); if the end-2014 ratio is already lower, hold that ratio
parameters.adjustment_path: loose in shape: CAPB follows projections to 2015, adjusts gradually 2016-2020 (the document says 'gradually'; the gold takes a linear path), constant 2020-2030 (gold holds the 2015 CAPB at its 2014 value)
parameters.interest_growth_differential: strict rule: rises linearly from its 2014 level to 1 percentage point by 2028 and stays there; the 2014 starting level is data (gold uses WEO Oct 2025 outturn: interest on previous-year debt minus nominal GDP growth, not the 2014 projection)
parameters.scope: emerging markets only (the advanced-economy rule is not fully specified and is not reproducible)
parameters.vintage: WEO October 2025 for GDP and fiscal outturns; end-2014 debt and CAPB as printed in the Fiscal Monitor Statistical Table 14 and stated in the question
